issues.issue: Was drug trafficking a serious non-political crime under Article 1F(b), so that the RPD could exclude the applicant?
issues.applicant_position: Seriousness should be weighed against mitigating factors: he was forthcoming, only an accomplice, and never got the $50,000.
issues.respondent_position: Drug trafficking is a serious non-political crime; he was a party to the offence; no balancing is required.
issues.result_quote: His activity constituted a serious, non-political crime in Canada, in violation of subsection 5(1) of the CDSA.

issues.issue: Did the RPD have to balance aggravating and mitigating factors or consider the claimant's good character before excluding under Article 1F(b)?
issues.applicant_position: The RPD had to balance mitigating factors and good character before deciding exclusion.
issues.respondent_position: No balancing or good-character inquiry is required; mitigating factors are not salient.
issues.result_quote: There is no obligation or requirement on the RPD to conduct a “balancing” exercise to determine whether a claimant is excluded

issues.issue: Did the RPD consider the circumstances of the crime and the applicant's role in it?
issues.applicant_position: RPD failed to consider his forthcoming admission, accomplice role and the unpaid $50,000.
issues.respondent_position: RPD considered all circumstances on the evidence; applicant does not dispute the facts of his participation.
issues.result_quote: The RPD did, in fact, consider the circumstances of the seriousness of Mr. Murillo’s crime

issues.issue: Is Article 1F(b) limited to fugitives from justice, or does it require a specific crime to be attributed to the claimant (Pushpanathan, Zrig)?
issues.applicant_position: Article 1F(b) targets fugitives only; Pushpanathan supports him; no specific crime was attributed to him.
issues.respondent_position: Pushpanathan concerns Article 1F(c); Zrig requires no specific charge, only serious reasons for considering a serious non-political crime.
issues.result_quote: the Federal Court of Appeal explicitly rejected Mr. Murillo’s argument and confirmed that it is not necessary for a specific crime to be attributed to a claimant
